passages.text: The human stomach was long believed to be a sterile environment due to its extreme acidity (pH 1.5–3.5), which was considered incompatible with microbial survival. Standard medical teaching through the 1970s held that peptic ulcers were caused by excess gastric acid secretion, stress, and dietary factors, and were treated with antacids and lifestyle modification.
passages.source: Sleisenger & Fordtran's Gastrointestinal Disease, 3rd ed. (1978), Chapter 14

passages.text: The bacterium Helicobacter pylori (formerly Campylobacter pylori) is the causative agent of the majority of peptic ulcers and chronic gastritis. H. pylori colonizes the gastric mucosa in approximately 50% of the world's population. Infection is treatable with a combination of proton pump inhibitors and antibiotics (triple therapy). The discovery, by Barry Marshall and Robin Warren, was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 2005.
passages.source: Marshall, B.J. & Warren, J.R. (1984). 'Unidentified curved bacilli in the stomach of patients with gastritis and peptic ulceration.' The Lancet, 323(8390), 1311–1315; Nobel Committee Citation (2005)

Passage B states ulcers are caused by H. pylori bacterial infection and the stomach is not sterile. The passages directly contradict each other on both the sterility of the stomach and the etiology of peptic ulcers — a surface-level, explicitly stated temporal scientific conflict.
label.explanation: Passage A reflects the pre-1984 consensus that the stomach is sterile and ulcers are acid-driven. Passage B reflects the Nobel Prize-winning discovery that H. pylori bacteria cause most ulcers — a direct contradiction of both claims in Passage A.

passages.text: The neuron doctrine, as formulated by Santiago Ramón y Cajal and adopted as consensus by the early 20th century, holds that each neuron is an anatomically discrete cell with a complete cell membrane separating it from adjacent neurons. Electrical signals pass between neurons only at synapses and only in one direction — from the axon terminal of the presynaptic neuron to the dendrite of the postsynaptic neuron (Dale's Principle). Electrical coupling between neurons does not occur in the mature vertebrate nervous system.
passages.source: Cajal, S.R. (1911). Histologie du système nerveux de l'homme & des vertébrés. Madrid: Moya; Dale, H.H. (1935). Pharmacology and Nerve Endings, Proc. R. Soc. Med.

passages.text: Electrical synapses (gap junctions) are widespread in the adult vertebrate central nervous system. Gap junction channels formed by connexin proteins (primarily Cx36 in neurons) directly couple the cytoplasm of adjacent neurons, allowing bidirectional passage of ionic currents and small molecules. Electrical coupling plays critical roles in synchronizing oscillatory activity in interneuron networks throughout the neocortex, hippocampus, inferior olive, and retina in adult mammals.
passages.source: Connors, B.W. & Long, M.A. (2004). 'Electrical synapses in the mammalian brain.' Annual Review of Neuroscience, 27, 393–418.

input.question: Do these passages present a conflict, are they consistent, or is the relationship ambiguous?

Passage B states that electrical synapses are widespread in the adult vertebrate CNS and play critical functional roles. The passages directly and explicitly contradict each other — a surface-level conflict between early 20th-century doctrine and later empirical findings.
label.explanation: Passage A's categorical denial of adult vertebrate electrical synapses is directly contradicted by Passage B's experimental demonstration of widespread Cx36-based gap junctions in adult mammalian brain structures.

conflicting_spans.span: Electrical coupling between neurons does not occur in the mature vertebrate nervous system
Electrical synapses (gap junctions) are widespread in the adult vertebrate central nervous system

label.polarity_rationale: Evidence of electrical synapses refined the neuron doctrine and opened research into network synchronisation.

passages.text: The universe is static and eternal. The cosmological constant (Λ) introduced by Einstein into his field equations serves to balance the gravitational attraction of matter, yielding a universe of constant size and infinite age. Expansion or contraction of the universe is inconsistent with this formulation.
passages.source: Einstein, A. (1917). 'Kosmologische Betrachtungen zur allgemeinen Relativitätstheorie.' Sitzungsber. Preuss. Akad. Wiss., 142–152.

passages.text: The universe is expanding. Hubble's law (v = H₀d) demonstrates that galaxies recede from one another at velocities proportional to their separation, with Hubble constant H₀ ≈ 70 km/s/Mpc. This expansion implies the universe originated in a hot, dense state (the Big Bang) approximately 13.8 billion years ago and has been expanding ever since. Einstein later called the cosmological constant his 'greatest blunder.'
passages.source: Hubble, E. (1929). 'A Relation between Distance and Radial Velocity among Extra-Galactic Nebulae.' Proc. Nat. Acad. Sci. 15(3): 168–173; Planck Collaboration (2018), A&A 641, A6.

passages.text: Newtonian mechanics describes the propagation of light as governed by the medium through which it travels. In accordance with the luminiferous aether theory, the velocity of light should vary depending on the observer's motion relative to the aether. An observer moving at velocity v relative to the aether in the direction of light propagation should measure the speed of light as c − v.
passages.source: Maxwell, J.C. (1878). 'Ether.' Encyclopædia Britannica, 9th ed., Vol. 8; Michelson, A.A. (1881), pre-null-result era.

passages.text: The Michelson-Morley experiment (1887) measured the speed of light in two perpendicular directions as Earth moved through the putative aether. No fringe shift was detected. The null result has been confirmed to extraordinary precision by modern laser interferometry (Müller et al., 2003, Phys. Rev. Lett. 91:020401), establishing that the speed of light in vacuum is constant at c = 299,792,458 m/s regardless of the motion of the source or observer.
passages.source: Michelson, A.A. & Morley, E.W. (1887). 'On the Relative Motion of the Earth and of the Luminiferous Ether.' Am. J. Sci. 34: 333–345; Müller et al. (2003).

passages.text: Lamarckian inheritance proposes that traits acquired by an organism during its lifetime in response to environmental pressures are heritable by offspring. For example, a giraffe that stretches its neck to reach higher foliage will pass a longer neck to its progeny. Adaptive morphological changes induced by environmental experience are directly incorporated into the germline.
passages.source: Lamarck, J.-B. (1809). Philosophie Zoologique. Paris: Dentu.

passages.text: The central dogma of molecular biology (Crick, 1958) states that genetic information flows from DNA to RNA to protein. Somatic cells express proteins in response to environmental stimuli, but these protein-level changes do not alter the nucleotide sequence of germline DNA. The Weismann barrier — the separation of somatic and germline cell lineages — prevents somatic mutations and acquired phenotypic modifications from being transmitted to offspring through conventional heredity.
passages.source: Crick, F.H.C. (1958). 'On Protein Synthesis.' Symp. Soc. Exp. Biol. 12: 138–163; Weismann, A. (1892). Das Keimplasma.

The central dogma and Weismann barrier together establish that somatic cell phenotypic changes do not alter germline DNA sequence, and therefore cannot be transmitted to offspring via genetic inheritance — one inference step connects Lamarckism's required mechanism to the central dogma's prohibition of that mechanism.

CONFLICT — The Lamarckian mechanism (environmental modification → germline transmission) is ruled out by the central dogma's information flow (DNA → RNA → protein, not reverse) and the Weismann barrier, revealed in a single mechanistic inference.
label.explanation: One inference step — asking how somatic changes would enter the germline — reveals the direct mechanistic impossibility under the central dogma and Weismann barrier.

passages.text: Phlogiston theory (Stahl, 1703) holds that combustible materials contain a substance called phlogiston, which is released during burning. When wood burns, phlogiston is released into the air, and the residual ash is dephlogisticated wood. Air can become 'saturated' with phlogiston and will no longer support combustion. The more phlogiston a substance contains, the more readily and completely it burns.
passages.source: Stahl, G.E. (1703). Zymotechnia Fundamentalis. Halle.

passages.text: Lavoisier (1777–1783) demonstrated that combustion is a chemical reaction between a fuel and oxygen (O₂). The mass of combustion products equals the mass of reactants (conservation of mass). Metals that burn gain mass — they oxidize — which phlogiston theory predicts incorrectly (if phlogiston were released, the residue should be lighter, not heavier, than the metal). Modern chemistry identifies combustion products (CO₂, H₂O, metal oxides) as compounds formed by reaction with atmospheric oxygen.
passages.source: Lavoisier, A.-L. (1783). 'Réflexions sur le phlogistique.' Mémoires de l'Académie Royale des Sciences.

input.question: Do these passages present a conflict, are they consistent, or is the relationship ambiguous?

reasoning_chain: Step 1 — Phlogiston theory predicts that a burning substance loses phlogiston, so the residue should weigh less than the original material. Applying this to metal combustion (calcination): the calx (metal oxide) should weigh less than the original metal. Lavoisier's experimental finding is that metal calxes weigh more than the original metals — a result that directly falsifies the phlogiston prediction in a single inference step (mass comparison).

CONFLICT — One inference step — applying phlogiston's mass prediction to metal oxidation — reveals the theory predicts a mass decrease where Lavoisier's experiments consistently measured a mass increase.
label.explanation: One inference step connecting phlogiston's release mechanism to conservation of mass exposes the theory's falsification: burning metals gain mass (they react with oxygen), whereas phlogiston theory predicts mass loss.

label.polarity_rationale: Lavoisier's mass measurements against phlogiston theory founded modern combustion chemistry.

passages.text: The steady-state theory of cosmology (Hoyle, Bondi & Gold, 1948) proposes that the universe has no beginning and no end. As the universe expands, new matter is continuously created to maintain a constant average density. The universe is homogeneous and isotropic on large scales and has always appeared the same at all cosmic epochs — the 'perfect cosmological principle.'
passages.source: Bondi, H. & Gold, T. (1948). 'The Steady-State Theory of the Expanding Universe.' MNRAS 108: 252–270; Hoyle, F. (1948). MNRAS 108: 372–382.

passages.text: The cosmic microwave background (CMB) is a near-uniform thermal radiation field permeating all of space with a current temperature of 2.725 K, first detected by Penzias and Wilson (1965) and mapped in detail by the COBE, WMAP, and Planck satellites. The CMB's blackbody spectrum and spatial uniformity are explained by the Big Bang model as the cooled relic of a hot, dense early universe approximately 380,000 years after the Big Bang. The CMB temperature scales as T ∝ (1+z) with redshift z.
passages.source: Penzias, A.A. & Wilson, R.W. (1965). ApJ 142: 419–421; Planck Collaboration (2018), A&A 641, A1.

reasoning_chain: Step 1 — The steady-state theory's perfect cosmological principle requires that the universe has always appeared the same at all epochs — meaning the large-scale properties of the universe at any past cosmic epoch must be identical to those today.

Step 2 — The CMB temperature scales as T ∝ (1+z), meaning at redshift z = 1000 (early universe) the CMB temperature was ~2725 K, not 2.725 K. A universe that has always looked the same would predict a CMB temperature of 2.725 K at all epochs — but the T ∝ (1+z) scaling directly implies the early universe was vastly hotter and denser, making the universe's appearance radically different at high redshift. This falsifies the 'always the same' requirement of steady-state theory.

CONFLICT — Two inference steps — applying the perfect cosmological principle to CMB temperature evolution, and then computing the implied early-universe temperature — reveal the steady-state theory predicts an impossibility contradicted by the CMB's observed temperature-redshift relation.
label.explanation: Two inference steps are needed: first, the steady-state perfect cosmological principle requires epoch-invariant appearance; second, CMB's T ∝ (1+z) scaling proves the early universe was orders-of-magnitude hotter, violating that requirement.

perfect cosmological principle
CMB temperature scales as T ∝ (1+z) with redshift z

label.polarity_rationale: The CMB's temperature–redshift relation decided the steady-state versus Big Bang debate and advanced observational cosmology.

passages.text: Neoclassical neuroscience held that adult mammalian brains are incapable of neurogenesis — the production of new neurons. Following development, the brain's complement of neurons is fixed; neuron death is permanent and irreplaceable. This view, dominant from the mid-20th century through the 1980s, supported the general clinical conclusion that adult brain injuries producing neuron loss (stroke, TBI) are necessarily permanent in their neuronal component.
passages.source: Rakic, P. (1985). 'Limits of neurogenesis in primates.' Science 227(4690): 1054–1056.

passages.text: Adult neurogenesis occurs in at least two regions of the mammalian brain: the subventricular zone (SVZ) of the lateral ventricles and the subgranular zone (SGZ) of the dentate gyrus in the hippocampus. In rodents, thousands of new neurons are generated daily in these regions. Adult neurogenesis in the human hippocampus has been confirmed by ¹⁴C-dating of neuronal DNA, with an annual turnover rate of ~1.75% of dentate gyrus neurons.
passages.source: Eriksson, P.S. et al. (1998). 'Neurogenesis in the adult human hippocampus.' Nature Medicine 4: 1313–1317; Spalding, K.L. et al. (2013). 'Dynamics of hippocampal neurogenesis in adult humans.' Cell 153(6): 1219–1227.

reasoning_chain: Step 1 — Passage A asserts that adult mammalian neurons cannot be replaced, meaning any neuronal cell death is permanent. Passage B establishes that adult human hippocampal neurogenesis occurs at ~1.75% annual turnover, meaning new neurons are generated to replace lost ones in the dentate gyrus.

Step 2 — If new neurons are generated in the adult human hippocampus at measurable rates (1.75%/year), then the claim that adult mammalian brains are 'incapable of neurogenesis' is falsified — specifically because the same mammalian taxon (humans) for which Rakic generalized the claim demonstrates the opposite. The clinical conclusion that adult brain injuries are necessarily permanent in their neuronal component is also falsified for hippocampal injuries.

CONFLICT — Two inference steps — applying the no-neurogenesis claim to the human hippocampus specifically, and then checking it against the carbon-dated neuronal turnover data — expose the direct contradiction.
label.explanation: Two inference steps are needed: extrapolating the 'no adult neurogenesis' claim to human hippocampus, and verifying it against ¹⁴C-dated neuronal turnover data showing 1.75% annual replacement.

label.polarity_rationale: Evidence of adult neurogenesis revised a fixed-neuron dogma and opened new avenues for brain-injury research.

passages.text: The classical view of protein folding (Anfinsen's dogma, 1973) holds that the three-dimensional structure of a protein is uniquely and entirely determined by its amino acid sequence. Under physiological conditions, a polypeptide spontaneously and reproducibly folds into its native functional conformation without the assistance of any other macromolecule. The native state corresponds to the thermodynamic free-energy minimum of the folding landscape.
passages.source: Anfinsen, C.B. (1973). 'Principles that Govern the Folding of Protein Chains.' Science 181(4096): 223–230. Nobel Lecture.

passages.text: Molecular chaperones (e.g., Hsp70, Hsp60/GroEL-GroES, Hsp90) are required for the correct folding of a significant fraction of cellular proteins in vivo. Chaperones prevent aggregation of nascent polypeptides as they emerge from the ribosome, actively facilitate folding of kinetically trapped intermediates, and are essential for the viability of all known cellular organisms. For many substrate proteins, the native fold cannot be reached without chaperone assistance under physiological crowding conditions.
passages.source: Hartl, F.U. & Hayer-Hartl, M. (2009). 'Converging concepts of protein folding in vitro and in vivo.' Nature Structural & Molecular Biology 16: 574–581.

input.question: Do these passages present a conflict, are they consistent, or is the relationship ambiguous?

reasoning_chain: Step 1 — Anfinsen's dogma states proteins fold spontaneously to their native state 'without the assistance of any other macromolecule' — this is the defining claim. Passage B states that many proteins cannot reach their native fold without chaperone assistance under physiological conditions.

Step 2 — Chaperones are macromolecules (proteins). If a subset of cellular proteins cannot achieve their native fold under physiological conditions without chaperone assistance, then Anfinsen's claim that no macromolecular assistance is required under physiological conditions is falsified for that subset — two inference steps connect the subset claim to the general principle's falsification.

CONFLICT — Two inference steps expose the conflict: identifying chaperones as the 'other macromolecules' Anfinsen excludes, and recognizing that their necessity for a significant protein fraction directly falsifies the universality of Anfinsen's dogma under in vivo conditions.
label.explanation: Two inference steps: recognizing that chaperones are macromolecules, and then recognizing that necessity of chaperones for a significant protein fraction contradicts the dogma's universal claim of sequence-sufficient autonomous folding under physiological conditions.

label.polarity_rationale: The chaperone findings refined Anfinsen's dogma into a fuller in vivo account of protein folding.

passages.text: The miasma theory of disease (dominant through the mid-19th century) holds that epidemic diseases — including cholera, malaria, and the Black Death — are caused by 'bad air' arising from rotting organic matter, swamps, and filth. Disease prevention should focus on eliminating foul odors and improving ventilation. Geographic clustering of disease cases is explained by the spatial distribution of miasmatic sources.
passages.source: Farr, W. (1852). 'Report on the Mortality of Cholera in England, 1848–49.' General Register Office, London.

passages.text: John Snow's investigation of the 1854 Broad Street cholera outbreak in London identified a contaminated water pump as the source of the epidemic. Snow mapped 616 cholera deaths and found that cases clustered around the Broad Street pump regardless of proximity to putative miasmatic sources (e.g., a nearby brewery whose workers did not contract cholera because they drank beer rather than pump water). Removing the pump handle ended the outbreak. Snow's work, combined with Koch's isolation of Vibrio cholerae in 1883, established cholera as a waterborne bacterial disease.
passages.source: Snow, J. (1855). On the Mode of Communication of Cholera, 2nd ed. London: Churchill; Koch, R. (1883). Berliner Klinische Wochenschrift.

input.question: Do these passages present a conflict, are they consistent, or is the relationship ambiguous?

reasoning_chain: Step 1 — Miasma theory predicts that cholera cases should cluster near sources of rotting matter and foul air, and that people exposed to the same air mass should have similar disease rates.

Step 2 — Snow's spatial analysis found that cholera cases clustered around the Broad Street water pump, not around identified miasmatic sources. The brewery workers — exposed to the same air but drinking different water — were unaffected, directly violating miasma theory's air-exposure prediction.

Step 3 — If disease risk is determined by the specific water source consumed rather than the ambient air quality, then the causal mechanism must be waterborne (a contaminant in the water) rather than airborne — and Koch's subsequent isolation of Vibrio cholerae from contaminated water confirms a bacterial pathogen transmitted through fecal-oral contamination, not air. This three-step chain makes the miasmatic causal mechanism not merely incomplete but fundamentally incorrect.

CONFLICT — Three inference steps — applying miasma's spatial prediction to Snow's map, identifying the brewery anomaly as a decisive air-exposure control, and inferring a waterborne bacterial mechanism — expose the theory as causally and mechanistically wrong.
label.explanation: Three inference steps are required: deriving miasma's spatial prediction, applying it to the Broad Street data (including the brewery control group), and inferring the waterborne bacterial mechanism that the data necessitates.

conflicting_spans.span: epidemic diseases are caused by 'bad air' arising from rotting organic matter
Disease prevention should focus on eliminating foul odors
cases clustered around the Broad Street pump regardless of proximity to putative miasmatic sources
nearby brewery whose workers did not contract cholera because they drank beer rather than pump water
cholera as a waterborne bacterial disease

label.polarity_rationale: Snow's data against miasma theory established waterborne transmission and modern epidemiology.

passages.text: Classical cardiovascular physiology held that the heart muscle (myocardium) is a terminally differentiated, post-mitotic tissue incapable of regeneration. Adult cardiomyocytes do not divide. Following a myocardial infarction, lost cardiomyocytes are replaced entirely by fibrotic scar tissue (collagen), not by new functional muscle cells. This is the basis for the permanent loss of cardiac function following heart attacks and the irreversibility of heart failure.
passages.source: Anversa, P. et al. (1991). 'Myocyte cell loss and myocyte hypertrophy in the aging rat heart.' J. Am. Coll. Cardiol. 18(5): 1441–1448 (pre-revision consensus statement section).

passages.text: Carbon-14 retrospective birth-dating of cardiomyocyte DNA (exploiting the atmospheric ¹⁴C pulse from nuclear weapons testing) demonstrates that human cardiomyocytes are renewed throughout adult life, with an annual renewal rate of approximately 1% at age 25, declining to ~0.45% by age 75. Approximately 45% of cardiomyocytes present at age 75 were generated after birth. Cardiac progenitor cells (c-Kit+ and Sca-1+ populations) have been identified in the adult heart, though their regenerative capacity remains under investigation.
passages.source: Bergmann, O. et al. (2009). 'Evidence for Cardiomyocyte Renewal in Humans.' Science 324(5923): 98–102.

reasoning_chain: Step 1 — Passage A claims that adult cardiomyocytes do not divide and lost cells are replaced only by fibrotic scar, implying zero cardiomyocyte renewal after development — a renewal rate of exactly 0%.

Step 2 — Passage B's ¹⁴C data establishes renewal rates of ~1%/year at age 25 and ~0.45%/year at age 75, with ~45% of a 75-year-old's cardiomyocytes having been generated post-birth. These renewal rates are nonzero, directly falsifying the zero-renewal claim.

Step 3 — If approximately 45% of cardiomyocytes in a 75-year-old were generated post-birth, then the claim that myocardial infarction damage cannot be repaired by new cardiomyocyte generation is not universally true; the heart has a measurable (if limited) regenerative mechanism. The classical model's clinical conclusion — that fibrotic replacement is the only possible response to cardiomyocyte loss — is therefore an overstated generalization contradicted by the renewal data.

CONFLICT — Three inference steps — computing the implied renewal rate from Passage A, comparing it to the ¹⁴C-derived nonzero renewal rate, and inferring the falsification of the fibrosis-only repair model — expose the conflict.
label.explanation: Three inference steps: Passage A implies 0% renewal, ¹⁴C data shows nonzero renewal rates, and the 45% post-birth cardiomyocyte fraction falsifies the 'fibrosis is the only repair mechanism' claim derived from the zero-renewal assumption.

conflicting_spans.span: Adult cardiomyocytes do not divide

annual renewal rate of approximately 1% at age 25
approximately 45% of cardiomyocytes present at age 75 were generated after birth

label.polarity_rationale: Evidence of cardiomyocyte renewal overturned the post-mitotic heart model and launched cardiac regeneration research.

passages.text: Malthus's principle of population (1798) predicts that human population grows geometrically (exponentially) while food production grows arithmetically (linearly). As a consequence, population will always tend to outrun food supply, and the natural checks on population — famine, disease, and war — are inevitable and recurrent. Sustained improvement in living standards for the general population is impossible because any gains are rapidly offset by population growth.
passages.source: Malthus, T.R. (1798). An Essay on the Principle of Population. London: J. Johnson.

passages.text: Global agricultural output has grown faster than world population since 1961. The Green Revolution (1960s–1980s) achieved 2–3× yield increases for wheat, rice, and maize through high-yielding variety breeding, synthetic fertilizers, and irrigation. Global per-capita food supply increased from approximately 2,200 kcal/person/day in 1961 to over 2,900 kcal/person/day by 2020, while world population grew from 3 billion to 8 billion over the same period. The demographic transition model predicts that fertility rates decline as living standards rise, breaking the Malthusian coupling between wealth and population growth.
passages.source: FAO (2022). The State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World; Borlaug, N.E. (1970). Nobel Peace Prize Lecture; UN Population Division (2022).

Step 3 — Malthus's model also predicts that improvements in living standards are unsustainable because they stimulate population growth, restoring poverty. The demographic transition model (Passage B) predicts and documents the opposite: rising living standards reduce fertility rates, breaking the feedback loop Malthus assumed. The empirical fertility decline in developed nations directly falsifies Malthus's coupling assumption.

passages.text: The classical theory of special relativity (Einstein, 1905) requires that no object with mass can be accelerated to or beyond the speed of light c, because the relativistic mass m = γm₀ (where γ = 1/√(1−v²/c²)) diverges to infinity as v → c, requiring infinite energy for further acceleration. Faster-than-light (FTL) travel for massive particles is therefore physically impossible. Causality is preserved: no signal or influence can propagate faster than c.
passages.source: Einstein, A. (1905). 'Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper.' Annalen der Physik 17: 891–921.

Subsequent investigation identified two hardware faults: a loose fiber-optic cable connector and an oscillator running at an incorrect frequency. After correction, the neutrino arrival time was consistent with c.

passages.text: The standard model of particle physics treats the neutrino as a massless particle (in its original formulation). Neutrinos come in three flavors: electron (νₑ), muon (νμ), and tau (ντ). Because neutrinos are massless, their flavor is a conserved quantum number — an electron neutrino produced in a nuclear reaction remains an electron neutrino indefinitely, and the three flavors are completely distinct species with no inter-conversion.

passages.text: The Super-Kamiokande experiment (Fukuda et al., 1998) observed a deficit in the atmospheric muon neutrino flux and demonstrated that νμ oscillate into ντ with mixing angle θ₂₃ ≈ 45° and squared mass difference Δm²₂₃ ≈ 2.5 × 10⁻³ eV². Solar neutrino oscillations (SNO, 2001–2002) confirmed νₑ → νμ/ντ transitions. Neutrino oscillation is only possible if neutrinos have nonzero mass, which requires physics beyond the Standard Model. The 2015 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded for this discovery.
passages.source: Fukuda, Y. et al. [Super-Kamiokande] (1998). Phys. Rev. Lett. 81: 1562–1567; Ahmad, Q.R. et al. [SNO] (2002). Phys. Rev. Lett. 89: 011301.

passages.text: The classical theory of black holes (Hawking, 1967–1974) holds that black holes are perfect absorbers with an event horizon from which nothing — including information — can escape. A black hole is fully characterized by only three external parameters: mass (M), charge (Q), and angular momentum (J) — the 'no-hair theorem.' All information about the infalling matter is permanently destroyed when it crosses the event horizon and is lost from the observable universe.
passages.source: Hawking, S.W. (1974). 'Black hole explosions?' Nature 248: 30–31; Wheeler, J.A. (1971). 'Adding the 'L' to physics.' Lecture (no-hair theorem).

passages.text: Hawking radiation: a black hole of mass M radiates thermally with a Hawking temperature T_H = ℏc³/(8πGMk_B). Over time, a black hole loses mass through this radiation and eventually evaporates completely. The radiation is precisely thermal — it has no correlations that encode the quantum state of the infalling matter. Because thermal radiation carries no information, the final state after complete evaporation is a thermal bath with maximal entropy, regardless of the initial state — this is the black hole information paradox (Hawking, 1976).
passages.source: Hawking, S.W. (1976). 'Breakdown of predictability in gravitational collapse.' Phys. Rev. D 14: 2460–2473.

reasoning_chain: Step 1 — The no-hair theorem (Passage A) states that a black hole is fully characterized by M, Q, J — meaning all other information about infalling matter is destroyed at the horizon, consistent with general relativity's classical framework.

Step 2 — Hawking radiation (Passage B) demonstrates that black holes are not perfect absorbers but rather emit thermal radiation with T_H = ℏc³/(8πGMk_B) and evaporate over time — a quantum mechanical effect absent from classical GR.

Step 3 — Because Hawking radiation is purely thermal (a blackbody spectrum with no correlations), it carries zero information about the initial quantum state of the infalling matter. Over the full evaporation lifetime, the pure initial quantum state of infalling matter maps to a mixed thermal final state.

Step 4 — In quantum mechanics, the fundamental postulate of unitarity requires that the evolution of a closed quantum system always maps pure states to pure states (no information is destroyed). A pure initial state cannot evolve into a mixed thermal state under unitary evolution.

Step 5 — This creates an irreducible conflict: if general relativity (no-hair theorem) and Hawking radiation are both correct, quantum unitarity is violated — a fundamental postulate of quantum mechanics fails. If quantum mechanics (unitarity) and Hawking radiation are both correct, the information must escape encoded in subtle correlations in the Hawking radiation — but Passage B explicitly states the radiation is precisely thermal with no such correlations. At least one of {GR/no-hair, Hawking radiation thermal purity, quantum unitarity} must be wrong, but none can be abandoned without destroying a major theoretical framework — a conflict that requires five inference steps to fully develop.

CONFLICT — Five inference steps — no-hair's information destruction, Hawking radiation's quantum origin, thermal radiation's information-free spectrum, quantum mechanics' unitarity requirement, and the three-way impossibility — reveal the black hole information paradox as a deep irresolvable conflict between general relativity and quantum mechanics that, five decades after its formulation, remains one of the central unsolved problems in theoretical physics.
label.explanation: Five inference steps trace the conflict from the no-hair theorem through Hawking radiation, thermal purity, quantum unitarity, and the three-way incompatibility — constituting the famous black hole information paradox.

passages.text: The somatic mutation theory of cancer (SMT) holds that cancer arises from the accumulation of somatic mutations in genes that control cell proliferation (proto-oncogenes) and cell death (tumor suppressor genes). The sequence of mutation acquisition — e.g., APC → KRAS → SMAD4 → TP53 in colorectal cancer — drives progressive malignant transformation. Cancer is fundamentally a disease of the genome: heritable genetic alterations in single cells are the necessary and sufficient cause of tumorigenesis. The tumor microenvironment and tissue context are secondary.

passages.text: The tissue organization field theory (TOFT) proposes that cancer is primarily a tissue-level disease — a disruption of normal tissue architecture and cell-cell signaling rather than a cell-autonomous genomic disease. Evidence: (1) Normal nuclei transplanted into enucleated frog eggs develop normally despite containing mutations. (2) Cancer cells placed in normal tissue contexts can revert to normal behavior (Bissell et al.). (3) Non-mutagenic carcinogens (e.g., estrogen, asbestos) promote cancer through epigenetic and microenvironmental mechanisms without introducing driver mutations. (4) Many cells with classic driver mutations (e.g., KRAS G12D in pancreatic ductal cells) never progress to cancer in the absence of specific tissue signals.
passages.source: Soto, A.M. & Sonnenschein, C. (2011). 'The tissue organization field theory of cancer.' BioEssays 33(5): 332–340; Bissell, M.J. & Hines, W.C. (2011). Nature Medicine 17: 320–329.

passages.text: The Copenhagen interpretation of quantum mechanics (Bohr, Heisenberg, 1920s–1930s) holds that a quantum system does not possess definite values of observable properties prior to measurement. The wavefunction ψ represents the complete description of reality. Upon measurement, the wavefunction instantaneously 'collapses' to an eigenstate of the measured observable. The collapse is non-unitary, irreversible, and occurs only when a measurement is performed by a classical apparatus or observer. Between measurements, the system evolves unitarily according to the Schrödinger equation.
passages.source: Bohr, N. (1928). 'The Quantum Postulate and the Recent Development of Atomic Theory.' Nature 121: 580–590; Heisenberg, W. (1927). Z. Phys. 43: 172.

passages.text: Quantum decoherence theory (Zurek, 1981–2003; Joos & Zeh, 1985) demonstrates that a quantum system interacting with an environment of N degrees of freedom undergoes rapid loss of quantum coherence (off-diagonal density matrix elements) on a timescale τ_D ∝ (λ_th/Δx)² × τ_R, where λ_th is the thermal de Broglie wavelength and Δx is the superposition separation. For macroscopic objects (Δx ~ 1 cm, T ~ 300 K), decoherence occurs in ~10⁻²³ seconds. Decoherence explains the appearance of classical definite outcomes without invoking a collapse postulate or a privileged observer/apparatus boundary; the preferred basis ('pointer states') is selected by the environment, not by measurement.
passages.source: Zurek, W.H. (1981). Phys. Rev. D 24: 1516; Zurek, W.H. (2003). Rev. Mod. Phys. 75: 715; Joos, E. & Zeh, H.D. (1985). Z. Phys. B 59: 223.

reasoning_chain: Step 1 — Copenhagen (Passage A) requires a sharp, fundamental distinction between the classical measuring apparatus/observer and the quantum system being measured. The collapse is triggered by this boundary — the measurement postulate is irreducible and not derivable from unitary Schrödinger evolution alone.

Step 2 — Decoherence theory (Passage B) shows that the apparent collapse of the wavefunction arises from entanglement with environmental degrees of freedom — a fully unitary process described by the Schrödinger equation. No special observer, apparatus, or non-unitary collapse postulate is required.

Step 3 — For macroscopic objects at room temperature, decoherence occurs in ~10⁻²³ seconds — so fast that quantum superpositions of macroscopic states are destroyed by environmental entanglement long before any human observer interacts with the system. The observer therefore plays no causal role in the collapse.

Step 4 — Copenhagen treats wavefunction collapse as a fundamental, non-unitary dynamical law that supplements the Schrödinger equation. Decoherence theory shows that no such supplemental law is needed — the appearance of collapse emerges from unitary dynamics alone. If decoherence is correct, the collapse postulate is redundant; if Copenhagen is correct and collapse is a primitive irreducible law, decoherence provides only an approximation, not a derivation.

Step 5 — The two frameworks make mutually exclusive ontological claims about the completeness of the wavefunction description. Copenhagen holds that ψ is complete and collapse creates a definite outcome. Decoherence-based interpretations hold that ψ remains complete and unitary but the apparent collapse is perspectival — multiple branches coexist. Either definite outcomes are created by non-unitary collapse (Copenhagen) or they are not (decoherence/Everett). These ontologies are mutually exclusive.

CONFLICT — Five inference steps trace the conflict from Copenhagen's measurement boundary, through decoherence's derivation of apparent collapse from unitary dynamics, through the observer's causal irrelevance at 10⁻²³ s timescales, to the redundancy of the collapse postulate, and finally to the incompatible ontological claims — a foundational conflict in quantum foundations that remains unresolved.
label.explanation: Five inference steps expose the foundational conflict between Copenhagen's non-unitary collapse postulate and decoherence theory's derivation of apparent collapse from purely unitary environmental entanglement, culminating in incompatible ontological claims about the nature of quantum measurement.

label.polarity_rationale: Decoherence's challenge to the collapse postulate sharpened the measurement problem and advanced quantum foundations.

passages.text: The amyloid cascade hypothesis of Alzheimer's disease (Hardy & Higgins, 1992) proposes that the initiating pathological event is the abnormal accumulation of amyloid-β (Aβ) peptide, forming senile plaques. Aβ aggregation leads sequentially to neurofibrillary tangle formation, neuroinflammation, synapse loss, and neuronal death. The implication is that reducing Aβ production or clearing Aβ aggregates should halt disease progression.
passages.source: Hardy, J.A. & Higgins, G.A. (1992). 'Alzheimer's disease: the amyloid cascade hypothesis.' Science 256(5054): 184–185.

passages.text: Several anti-amyloid immunotherapies (aducanumab, lecanemab, donanemab) have achieved significant Aβ plaque clearance in clinical trials. Lecanemab (CLARITY-AD, 2023) and donanemab (TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2, 2023) demonstrated statistically significant slowing of clinical decline (27% and 35% slowing, respectively, on primary endpoints) compared to placebo in early Alzheimer's disease, with amyloid clearance confirmed by PET imaging. Both received FDA approval. Amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA) were observed as a significant adverse effect in ~20–35% of treated patients.
passages.source: van Dyck, C.H. et al. (2023). NEJM 388: 9–21 (lecanemab); Sims, J.R. et al. (2023). NEJM 389: 9–23 (donanemab).

Neither confirms nor refutes the strong form of the cascade hypothesis.

Step 3 — The passages are neither fully consistent (the cascade hypothesis predicted efficacy that would halt progression, not merely slow it modestly) nor clearly in conflict (modest slowing is consistent with Aβ playing a causal but not exclusive role). The relationship is genuinely ambiguous: the trials provide partial evidence for and against the hypothesis simultaneously.

AMBIGUOUS — The clinical trial results partially validate and partially undermine the amyloid cascade hypothesis; the relationship cannot be classified as consistent or conflicting without additional information about whether the modest effect size represents the hypothesis's prediction or its partial falsification.
label.ambiguity_reason: The 2023 clinical trial results show modest but significant clinical slowing, which is consistent with a weak form of the amyloid cascade hypothesis but inconsistent with its stronger form (clearance should halt progression). Whether this constitutes support, partial falsification, or delayed-treatment artifact is genuinely underdetermined by the available evidence.

passages.text: The gut microbiome (comprising ~10¹³ bacteria, archaea, fungi, and viruses) influences host metabolism, immune system development, and brain function via the gut-brain axis (involving the vagus nerve, enteric nervous system, and microbial metabolites including short-chain fatty acids, neurotransmitter precursors, and immune mediators). Dysbiosis — disruption of normal microbiome composition — has been associated with obesity, inflammatory bowel disease, depression, and autism spectrum disorder.
passages.source: Cryan, J.F. et al. (2019). 'The Microbiota-Gut-Brain Axis.' Physiological Reviews 99(4): 1877–2013.

passages.text: A 2022 meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials of probiotic supplementation for depression (32 RCTs, n = 2,456) found a statistically significant but small effect size (SMD = −0.34, 95% CI −0.49 to −0.19) on depressive symptom scales, with high heterogeneity (I² = 74%) across studies. Effect sizes were not significantly larger in studies with microbiome compositional data confirming dysbiosis at baseline. The clinical significance of the effect and its mechanistic basis remain uncertain.
passages.source: Ng, Q.X. et al. (2022). 'A systematic review and meta-analysis of the effects of probiotic supplementation on depression.' Journal of Affective Disorders 320: 402–414.

passages.text: The dark matter hypothesis holds that approximately 27% of the universe's energy density consists of non-baryonic dark matter — particles that interact gravitationally but not electromagnetically. Evidence includes galactic rotation curves (Rubin & Ford, 1970), gravitational lensing observations (Bullet Cluster, 2006), and the CMB power spectrum. The leading dark matter candidate is the WIMP (Weakly Interacting Massive Particle) with mass ~10–1000 GeV.
passages.source: Zwicky, F. (1933); Rubin, V. & Ford, W.K. (1970). ApJ 159: 379; Clowe, D. et al. (2006). ApJ Letters 648: L109.

passages.text: Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND, Milgrom 1983) proposes that the anomalous galactic rotation curves attributed to dark matter are instead explained by a modification of Newtonian gravity below an acceleration threshold a₀ ≈ 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁰ m/s². MOND accurately predicts rotation curves of individual galaxies and satisfies the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation, but struggles to explain cluster-scale lensing, the Bullet Cluster observations, and CMB acoustic peaks without invoking some form of additional matter.
passages.source: Milgrom, M. (1983). 'A modification of the Newtonian dynamics as a possible alternative to the hidden mass hypothesis.' ApJ 270: 365–370; Famaey, B. & McGaugh, S.S. (2012). Living Reviews in Relativity 15: 10.

reasoning_chain: Step 1 — The dark matter hypothesis (Passage A) explains galactic rotation curves, lensing, and the CMB by invoking a new class of non-baryonic particles. MOND (Passage B) proposes a gravitational modification that explains galactic rotation curves without new particles.

Step 2 — The two frameworks are in direct competition for explaining galactic rotation curves specifically — but each has distinct domains of success: MOND succeeds at galaxy scales, dark matter succeeds at cluster and cosmological scales. Neither is universally superior.

Step 3 — The Bullet Cluster observation (Passage A) is often cited as a definitive falsification of MOND (spatial separation of mass and gas), but Passage B acknowledges that MOND 'struggles' with this — meaning MOND proponents accept this as a challenge, not a refutation (some versions of MOND/TeVeS can partially accommodate it). The relationship between the passages is therefore ambiguous: they conflict on galactic-scale mechanism but neither can be declared correct or incorrect without additional theoretical specification and empirical evidence.

AMBIGUOUS — The passages represent competing research programs with overlapping and non-overlapping domains of empirical success; which framework is 'correct' for which observations is an active scientific debate, and the relationship cannot be determined to be a clear conflict or consistent coexistence without specifying the observational domain and the version of MOND under consideration.
label.ambiguity_reason: Dark matter and MOND are competing frameworks with partially overlapping evidence domains. MOND explains galactic rotation curves that dark matter also explains; dark matter explains the Bullet Cluster that MOND struggles with; neither framework is falsified across all domains simultaneously. The relationship is ambiguous: they conflict in claimed mechanism but not necessarily in all predictions, and which framework is empirically superior depends on the observational context.
